documents.title: SHSU Generative AI Guidance
documents.stance_why: The page states 'there is no defining university policy on AI' and 'It is up to each instructor to specify an AI policy for that particular class', so it sets no stance itself and hands the decision to instructors; it offers no named tiers.
documents.summary: A resource page with separate guidance for students, faculty and staff. It defers AI rules to each instructor, ties unauthorized or undisclosed use to the Academic Honesty Policy, cautions against AI detectors, and tells staff to use approved tools and protect data.

units.why: The student page says 'It is up to each instructor to specify an AI policy for that particular class', which hands the decision to instructors; P04 fits because no university rule is set.
units.anchor: It is up to each instructor to specify an AI policy for that particular class.

units.why: 'If you're not sure, ask!' tells students to check with professors, IT@SAM or the library when unsure, so P10 (ask before using AI).
units.anchor: If you’re not sure, ask!
units.frag_start: It is important to learn how

units.why: The sentence points students to IT@SAM and the library as human help; chosen P72 rather than P10 because it covers 'other questions' beyond whether a use is allowed.
units.anchor: you can reach out to IT@SAM or the library for other questions
units.frag_start: It is important to learn how
units.policy: Students can reach out to IT@SAM or the library for other questions about AI.

units.why: 'SHSU has access to Microsoft's Copilot, Gemini, and Google NotebookLM using your SHSU sign on' identifies licensed, sanctioned tools for students, so P17.
units.anchor: SHSU has access to Microsoft’s Copilot, Gemini, and Google NotebookLM using your SHSU sign on.

units.why: 'Using AI to complete work without permission may violate the university's Academic Honesty Policy' classes unpermitted AI use as possible misconduct, so P36.
units.anchor: Using AI to complete work without permission may violate the university’s
units.policy: Using AI to complete work without permission may violate the university's Academic Honesty Policy.
units.fit_note: Also implies that AI needs permission, but states it only as a possible violation ('may violate').

units.why: 'Always check with your instructor or supervisor before you use it' tells students to ask before using AI, so P10.
units.anchor: Always check with your instructor or supervisor before you use it.

units.why: 'Any assignments that allow the use of AI tools should include an acknowledgement of your AI use' sets disclosure for permitted use, so P24.
units.anchor: that allow the use of AI tools should include an acknowledgement of your AI use.

units.why: The page links 'How to Cite AI Generated Content' as help for disclosing AI; it is a pointer to citation guidance, so P24 rather than P25, since no required details are stated.
units.anchor: How to Cite AI Generated Content
units.fit_note: Only links to citation guidance; it does not state what a citation must contain.

units.why: 'the simple use of generative AI is not necessarily an academic integrity problem' sets a permissive baseline: use alone is not misconduct. P02 is the nearest type, though this is a framing and not an encouragement.
units.anchor: the simple use of generative AI is not necessarily an academic integrity problem
units.frag_start: Like any tool, AI may be
units.policy: The simple use of generative AI is not necessarily an academic integrity problem.
units.fit_note: States only that use is not automatically misconduct; it does not allow or encourage AI by default.

units.why: 'a student's undisclosed use of generative AI in assignments outside the boundaries that an instructor has set ... may constitute a violation' makes undisclosed, out-of-bounds use the violation (P28); P36 also fits but the disclosure element defines the violation here.
units.anchor: undisclosed use of generative AI in assignments outside the boundaries that an instructor has set
units.policy: A student's undisclosed use of generative AI in assignments outside the boundaries that an instructor has set for a specific course may constitute a violation of SHSU's Academic Honesty policy.
units.fit_note: The violation is undisclosed AND out-of-bounds use; it does not say disclosed in-bounds use is safe.

units.why: 'Instructors should make sure that students are informed of course expectations' tells instructors to communicate their AI rules and citation expectations, so P09.
units.anchor: Instructors should make sure that students are informed of course expectations
units.fit_note: Says to inform students of expectations, not specifically in the syllabus.

units.why: 'these detection tools are recognized as deeply flawed' with false positives and negatives says detectors are unreliable, so P39.
units.anchor: these detection tools are recognized as deeply flawed

units.why: The student ethics list gives 'Environmental Impact' (training uses significant energy) as an AI concern, so P53.
units.anchor: Training AI tools uses significant energy, raising concerns about sustainability.

units.why: 'AI tools can produce incorrect or misleading information. Always fact-check the outputs' tells students to verify output, so P31.
units.anchor: Always fact-check the outputs.
units.policy: Students always fact-check AI outputs, because AI tools can produce incorrect or misleading information.

units.why: 'AI models may reflect biases in their training data' names bias and tells students to use critical thinking; P53 chosen because the passage is about bias, with P31 a weaker fit.
units.anchor: AI models may reflect biases in their training data
units.policy: AI models may reflect biases in their training data, so students use critical thinking when analyzing their results.

units.why: 'Avoid sharing sensitive or personal information with AI tools' protects personal data, so P50.
units.anchor: Avoid sharing sensitive or personal information with AI tools
units.policy: Students avoid sharing sensitive or personal information with AI tools, as their data privacy policies may not fully protect the input.

units.why: 'SHSU has a contract with Copilot and Gemini to not use your information for training purposes' states vendor data protection for the licensed tools, so P50 (vetted tools); P65 is about institutional contract review, which is not described.
units.anchor: contract with Copilot and Gemini to not use your information for training purposes.
units.fit_note: Informs about the contract protection but does not tell students to prefer the tools.

units.why: The faculty page says 'there is no defining university policy on AI' and that AI is being integrated into existing policies; it describes the institution's framework (none, folded into Academic Honesty and Course Structure), so P56 with a fit note.
units.anchor: While there is no defining university policy on AI
units.policy: There is no defining university policy on AI; SHSU works to integrate AI practice into existing and proposed policies such as Academic Honesty and Course Structure and Management.
units.fit_note: Says no framework exists and that AI is being folded into existing policies; it states no purpose or principles.

units.why: 'living document' that stakeholders will crowdsource and grow signals the guidance will change and invites contributions, so P54.
units.anchor: This guide is designed to become a living document for the support of SHSU faculty
units.frag_end: best practices for AI in higher education settings.
units.policy: The faculty guide is designed to become a living document, a crowdsourced collection inviting contributions from stakeholders.

units.why: 'an emergent mandate from the state: integrate AI into classroom learning and student research projects' for workforce readiness gives the career rationale, so P44.
units.anchor: integrate AI into classroom learning and student research projects to help prepare students
units.policy: The university has an emergent mandate from the state to integrate AI into classroom learning and student research projects to help prepare students for workforce readiness.
units.fit_note: A state mandate to integrate AI, not only a statement that AI is a professional skill.

units.why: 'we remain true to our foundational commitment to guiding students through their intellectual development and acquisition of personal academic skills' states the skill-building side of the balance, so P41.
units.anchor: guiding students through their intellectual development and acquisition of personal academic skills
units.frag_start: At the same time, we remain true
units.fit_note: Commits to students' skill development but does not say AI shortcuts practice.

units.why: The page links syllabus statements ranging 'from a complete ban on AI tools to requiring the use of AI tools'; this supports instructor-set policy (P04) and does not itself require a syllabus statement, so not P09.
units.anchor: examples of syllabus statements that cover different types of AI policies
units.policy: The page offers links to syllabus statement examples covering policies from a complete ban on AI tools to requiring AI tools for specific activities or assignments.
units.fit_note: Provides model statements for instructors; the document does not itself require a syllabus statement.

units.why: 'Many of them also mention the rationale for the policy' points instructors to examples that give reasons, so P66.
units.anchor: Many of them also mention the rationale for the policy being followed.
units.fit_note: Notes that examples include a rationale; it does not tell instructors to explain their rules.

units.why: The faculty section adds 'Instructors should be cautious in relying on an AI detection tool', a faculty-specific caution beyond the student paragraph, so P39 (do not rely on detectors).
units.anchor: Instructors should be cautious in relying on an AI detection tool to take
units.frag_end: conclusive evidence that they did not use AI.
units.policy: Instructors should be cautious in relying on an AI detection tool to take any negative actions regarding student work, since a student would have difficulty providing conclusive evidence that they did not use AI.

units.why: 'educate them about the basics of how it actually works' recommends AI-literacy resources for course use, so P70 (student AI-literacy) rather than P63 (faculty support).
units.anchor: educate them about the basics of how it actually works, what it does well
units.policy: Instructors might add resources to a course that educate students about how generative AI works, what it does well or poorly, and the concerns with its use, to build a foundation of AI literacy.

units.why: The page lists AI resource pages from other universities for faculty, covering overviews, ethics and classroom use, which supports instructors in learning about AI, so P63.
units.anchor: helpful AI resource pages from other universities that cover everything from overviews
units.frag_start: Here are some helpful AI resource
units.policy: The page lists AI resource pages from other universities covering overviews of generative AI, ethical considerations, and classroom and research applications.

units.why: The page lists grant funding for generative AI research; this is support for AI research, not a rule about AI use and no existing type covers it, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: Here are some grant funding opportunities for research in generative AI
units.policy: The page lists grant funding opportunities for research in generative AI.
units.uncovered_note: The university points faculty to external grant funding for generative AI research.

units.why: 'Learn how instructors can work with AI in their teaching and research' sets who the faculty guidance serves and its scope, so P61 as a scope statement.
units.anchor: Learn how instructors can work with AI in their teaching and research.
units.fit_note: Describes who the guidance serves rather than defining AI.

units.why: The page defines generative AI as AI that 'can create new, original content such as text, images, audio, video, or code', setting a policy definition, so P61.
units.anchor: Generative AI (Gen AI) is a type of AI that can create new, original content
units.frag_end: in response to a user's prompt or request.
units.policy: Generative AI is a type of AI that can create new, original content such as text, images, audio, video, or code.

units.why: The guidance defines 'Traditional AI' as rule-based systems that do not learn from data, drawing a scope line against generative AI, so P61.
units.anchor: operates using explicitly programmed rules, logic, and manually created knowledge
units.policy: Traditional AI operates using explicitly programmed rules, logic, and manually created knowledge rather than learning from data.

units.why: The faculty-section definition 'AI refers to tools and systems that mimic human intelligence' is a separate definition from the general overview, so P61.
units.anchor: AI refers to tools and systems that mimic human intelligence
units.frag_start: AI refers to tools and systems

units.why: Listing GitHub Copilot among generative AI tools that 'auto-complete code' brings code assistants into the definition by example only, so P07 with a fit note.
units.anchor: GitHub Copilot that auto-complete code, suggest functions, or generate entire code snippets
units.policy: GitHub Copilot, which auto-completes code, suggests functions, or generates entire code snippets, is an example of generative AI.
units.fit_note: Names a coding assistant as an example of generative AI; sets no rule for editors or IDEs.

units.why: Staff section: 'encourages employees to use institutionally approved AI tools, such as Microsoft Copilot and Google Gemini' encourages use of vetted tools by staff, so P50 with unit_stance encourage.
units.anchor: encourages employees to use institutionally approved AI tools, such as Microsoft Copilot and Google Gemini
units.policy: SHSU encourages employees to use institutionally approved AI tools, such as Microsoft Copilot and Google Gemini, when engaging in university-related work.

units.why: 'avoid entering sensitive, confidential, or protected data into non-approved AI applications' restricts data entry into unvetted tools, so P50.
units.anchor: avoid entering sensitive, confidential, or protected data into non-approved AI applications
units.policy: Employees avoid entering sensitive, confidential, or protected data into non-approved AI applications not covered by university agreements and safeguards.

units.why: 'compliance with applicable regulations and policies, including FERPA, HIPAA, and institutional data governance requirements' ties approved AI use to law and policy, so P77.
units.anchor: including FERPA, HIPAA, and institutional data governance requirements
units.policy: Approved AI platforms are designed to better support compliance with FERPA, HIPAA, and institutional data governance requirements.

units.why: 'Always verify AI-generated content for accuracy and originality' tells staff to verify output, so P31.
units.anchor: Always verify AI-generated content for accuracy and originality.

units.why: 'Make sure to check with your supervisor before using an AI tool' tells staff to ask before use, so P10.
units.anchor: Make sure to check with your supervisor before using an AI tool.

units.why: 'There are some tasks for which AI may not be appropriate, ethical, or even legal' warns of inappropriate tasks without naming them; P77 is nearest because of 'legal'.
units.anchor: There are some tasks for which AI may not be appropriate, ethical, or even legal.
units.fit_note: Warns that some tasks are inappropriate, unethical or illegal without naming tasks or laws.

units.why: 'Generative AI can help brainstorm ideas, summarize readings, draft outlines, sort data' lists uses of AI for staff work, so P59.
units.anchor: Generative AI can help brainstorm ideas, summarize readings, draft outlines, sort data
units.fit_note: Covers staff work generally, not only teaching tasks.

units.why: 'Look into free tools like ChatGPT, DALL-E, or Grammarly's AI writing assistant' suggests free tools for staff to try, so P59 (encouraging use); it is not tied to vetting, unlike the approved-tools line.
units.anchor: Look into free tools like ChatGPT, DALL-E, or Grammarly’s AI writing assistant.
units.fit_note: Covers staff work generally, not only teaching tasks.

units.why: The staff ethics section repeats the privacy warning for employees without the SHSU contract line; the audience is different, so coded separately as P50.
units.anchor: Avoid sharing sensitive or personal information with AI tools, as their data privacy policies
units.policy: Employees avoid sharing sensitive or personal information with AI tools, as their data privacy policies may not fully protect the input.

units.why: The staff ethics section repeats the environmental concern for employees, a different audience, so P53.
units.anchor: Training AI tools uses significant energy

units.why: The prompt-writing advice 'focus on persona, task, context and format' teaches effective AI use as a skill, so P44.
units.anchor: When writing an AI prompt, focus on persona, task, context and format.
units.policy: When writing an AI prompt, staff focus on persona, task, context and format.

units.why: 'Run AI locally. Keep your data private. Maintain full control.' promotes local LLMs for privacy, so P50.
units.anchor: Run AI locally. Keep your data private. Maintain full control.
units.fit_note: Recommends local models for privacy, not university-vetted or licensed tools.

notes: Only one included document. The faculty section repeats the student-section academic-integrity paragraph; that exact repeat was not coded twice (only its added detector-caution sentence). Staff-section ethics lines were coded separately because the audience differs.
